text: The Belt and Road Initiative was described as a platform for transport connectivity but officials said standards and debt management would shape future cooperation.
Analysts said Chinese investment could support port development while lenders and governments may face pressure to improve transparency.
Beijing framed the initiative as shared growth but regional observers linked the projects to strategic competition and supply-chain influence.
ASEAN members may welcome infrastructure finance when rules procurement and dispute settlement are clear.
The report treated BRI participation as a managed opportunity with benefits tied to governance safeguards and regional trust.
